title: Gyorgy I Rakoczi to Istvan Racz (envoy in Turkey): letter in monoalphabetic letter cipher, not cracked
correspondents: Prince Gyorgy I Rakoczi -> Istvan Racz of Galospetri (Transylvanian ambassador at the Porte)
shelfmark: MNL OL E 190 (Archivum familiae Rakoczi), 43. doboz, 5. tetel, no. 597 (Lang C.Rag.05)
status: Lang: letters, monoalphabetic, "nincs feltorve". A prince writing his own cipher (Lang: both Rakoczi princes enciphered by hand).
why: Transylvanian-Ottoman diplomacy in the prince's own cipher; monoalphabetic and nearly complete, so a ciphertext-only break is plausible.
verify: Find the record in the E 190 database and any image; try monoalphabetic solution in Hungarian.
access_note: MNL OL E 190 database (descriptions, no page images located)

links.label: Lang 2015, Titkosirás a kora ujkori Magyarországon (MTA doctoral thesis, repertory pp. 191-330), p. 263

vetting_note: Still no image of MNL OL E 190 43. doboz 5. tétel no. 597, so it cannot be compared with Szilagyi 1883 no. 10. Chrome search of the MNL AdatbázisokOnline E 190 database (Rákóczi család levelezése): "Rácz Rákóczi" gives only Rácz István to Rácz János 1644 (box 12 no. 3865), Rákóczi to Rácz János 1648 (box 17 no. 5076) and Rácz István to Kassay, Constantinople 30 May 1642 (box 10 no. 3001); no Rákóczi to Rácz cipher letter of 1642, and no image. Lang's "43. doboz, 5. tétel" numbering (the cipher set) is outside the database's box/serial numbering. Lang repertory row C.Rag.05 re-read: "betűk, monoalf. | nincs feltörve | majdnem teljes". Needs a reproduction of no. 597 from MNL OL.
prior_unvetted: Ciphertext not seen (MNL OL E 190 43. doboz 5. tetel no. 597 is not imaged; the MNL database has no image) and a printed clear may exist: Szilagyi, Levelek es okiratok I. Rakoczy Gyorgy keleti osszekottetesei tortenetehez (1883, REAL-EOD 6176) no. 10, Rakoczi to Racz, Udvarhely 27 Apr 1642, pp. 665-668 (PDF pages 671-674), says 'Az czifrakkal valo irast magyarra megforditattuk ... megkuldtuk' and prints as its enclosure the Hungarian text of the cipher letter of Sebes, 19 Jan 1642, from Rakoczi's draft and a contemporary copy of the cipher ('A cursivval szedett egy egykoru masolat titkos irasabol van'). Racz (letters of 4 Mar and 15 May 1642, ibid. and Beke-Barabas 1888 pp. 583-585) could not read 'ket clavissal irt' letters (a reciprocal half-alphabet: 'az felso rend betuket az alsokon ... kell erteni') and sent them back, which is why a letter to Racz sits in the Rakoczi archive. Needs an image of no. 597 (MNL reading room or reproduction order) to compare with Szilagyi pp. 667-668 before any verdict; Lang 2015 p. 263 calls it 'nincs feltorve'.
